source_meta._title: Clicking a settings button when there's a slider under the mouse in the next screen plays the click sound twice

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running the first listed affected version, Minecraft 19w11a. Use desktop mouse input and the title-screen menus; no world, server, commands, cheats, seed, or multiplayer connection is required. Game audio must be routed to an audible output device.
preconditions: Launch a vanilla, unmodified Minecraft Java Edition client so that mods do not change menu behavior or GUI sounds.
Use Minecraft 19w11a, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 22w42a for this reproduction.
Ensure the operating system output device is unmuted and set to an audible level.
Ensure Minecraft's Master Volume is above 0%. If volume must be configured first, finish that configuration and return to the title screen before beginning the numbered procedure.
Use a physical mouse or an input device capable of keeping the left mouse button continuously depressed while the pointer is moved.
Begin on the fully loaded Minecraft title screen with the Options... button visible.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation configured for Minecraft 19w11a and start the game.
Wait for startup to finish. Do not continue while the loading screen is displayed or the client window is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The title screen is fully rendered, accepts mouse movement, and shows the Options... button.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer onto the center of the Options... button on the title screen. Do not press the mouse button yet.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is inside the Options... button and the button is visibly hovered.

steps.action: Press the left mouse button while the pointer is on Options..., and keep the physical mouse button continuously held down. Do not release it when the Options screen opens.
steps.exact_input: Left mouse button down; continue holding
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is visible while the left mouse button remains physically depressed.

steps.action: Without releasing the left mouse button, move the pointer upward from its current position and place it inside the rectangular FOV slider at the top of the Options screen. Target the slider control itself rather than nearby text or empty background.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse while continuing to hold the left mouse button
steps.success_cue: The Options screen remains open, the left mouse button is still held, and the pointer is visibly positioned within the FOV slider's bounds.

steps.action: With the pointer still positioned over the FOV slider, release the left mouse button once. Do not click again or move into another menu before handing off to observation.
steps.success_cue: The left mouse button has just been released over the FOV slider, and the Options screen remains the active screen.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just released the continuously held left mouse button while the pointer is over the FOV slider on the Options screen. Begin audio/UI observation immediately, without performing another click.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section; this plan uses the deterministic title-screen-to-FOV-slider procedure explicitly described in the report description and comments.

The operating system, window resolution, GUI Scale, and exact pixel coordinates are not specified. The executor must identify the destination slider by its FOV label rather than by fixed screen coordinates.
The report does not specify audio levels. Requiring an audible output device and Master Volume above 0% is a practical prerequisite for observing a sound-related issue.
The report states that the analogous cursor movement does not reproduce when entering Video Settings, so this plan deliberately uses the Options screen's FOV slider instead.
